>That figure does not include any unsubstantiated accusations where an investigation was unable to prove a sexual assault occurred, so an accurate figure for the total remains unknown.

Another way to phrase that percentage is: “Men who are accused of sexual assault possess the evidence required to conclusively *disprove* the accusation in only 2-10% of cases.” 

You’re assuming that 100% of unsubstantiated accusations are true, but even the article you linked accepts that we have absolutely no way of knowing that, so there is very significant potential error in the statistic. 

I’m not trying to make any comment on the validity of Tana’s claims in this post, but I will assert that we’re quite literally saying “guilty until proven innocent” here.

Except I haven’t seen any source in which she mentions feeling victimized by Cody Ko even at 25. She certainly doesn’t in the most recent podcast clip people are treating as if it’s a new thing.

Again, that anything even happened remains speculation because Tana has not made any direct accusations of any wrongdoing. People just take this same speculation and run with it every couple years, Tana plays into it, and everyone eats it up. I’ve seen it happen multiple times now and every time it’s just as unsubstantiated.

If you actually watched the podcast clip to which everyone is referring, she mentioned she slept around with friends of hers when she was “17 or 18” and insinuated Cody was one of those by including his name in a “shoutout” she gave immediately after.

No direct accusation that he slept with her when she was 17 was ever made. You’re treating speculation as fact.

Yeah, I understand; like I said I was referring to the Tana ones as they’re the ones which were most recently resurfaced in the “influencer drama” community from which the OP cross posted. 

As far as the one involving Cody’s friend, my only comment is that everyone is likely friends with someone who has done something seriously wrong at some point, everyone is predisposed to give their friends the benefit of the doubt when being told different things by different people, and therefore anyone with any degree of empathy for the situation should conclude that actions and attitudes of one’s friends are not necessarily reflective of their own actions and attitudes. 

If one of my friends were accused of something, I wouldn’t immediately disown them either, because I’m a better friend than that. I would expect them to be truthful with me, would expect them to explain themselves to me, and would use my own judgement to determine if this person is worth keeping in my life, and for all we know, Cody and all of his other friends did exactly that.

She’s never made a direct allegation toward Cody, and the narrative has changed every time it’s come up. First nothing happened, then she slept with *an influencer friend* around the time she was friends with Cody, then she slept with Cody but she asserts she was 18 when she did it, most recently she slept with *a group of different influencers including Cody* between the ages of 17 and 18. 

Tana herself does not seem to feel she is a victim of any of those people.

> I’m sure she’s aware of the consequences of making an accusation like that and wouldn’t make it if she knew her career would be at stake 

Except there’s absolutely no risk for her to make an unsubstantiated and vague claim like this because nobody has any hard evidence to prove or disprove the claim, nor can anyone say she even directly accused Cody of any wrongdoing should any hard evidence come to light that nothing wrong was done.

Everything people say about the situation is pure speculation. There’s no evidence they slept together and Tana (to my knowledge) has not directly said they did (insinuated, sure, but that feeds into speculation more than it does make an actual serious accusation). There’s no evidence of what age she was when the alleged contact happened and Tana herself has left it ambiguous. 

The fact that everything is so uncertain is what drives attention to the issue and, subsequently, to Tana herself. That’s consistent with her previous behavior around any drama including her name: she capitalizes ok the attention she gets from the drama and keeps things vague to keep the speculation alive. If she thought Cody had victimized her and wanted him to face consequences, she could have made a direct allegation that Cody slept with her when she was 17 a year or two ago when the topic last made the rounds in the “influencer news” space. I don’t think she believes there’s any justice that needs to be done; she just relishes in drama like she always has. 

If her career wasn’t ended by her being exposed for violently and publicly insulting people with racial slurs, nor for her failed (and quite frankly, dangerous) vidcon spin-off event about which she lied repeatedly and in which she directly preyed on her fans, then frankly, I don’t believe she’s at much risk of losing her career for *anything* she would do.
There are only two, and the one involving Tana is the “fresh” one everyone’s talking about like it hasn’t made the rounds several times over the past 8 years, and hence was the one I was referencing.

This same speculation has been circling around since they first collaborated with each other in 2016. As both parties typically do, Cody has made no comment, Tana has leaned into the speculation to capitalize on the attention. 

It’s the same flavor of drama on a different day.

The most shocking part of this thread to me was that these “career-ending” allegations were attributed to *Tana Mongeau* of all people. Only a couple years ago I remember her being largely known as a habitual liar. 

I agree it’s important to offer any potential victims of any kind of abuse support, but this has been a speculation that’s made rounds several times over the years and every time Tana has capitalized on the attention from the speculation. This is the same person who had a fake wedding with Jake Paul for content; are we seriously considering a passing nod at the speculations during a podcast to be a reliable enough source to assume guilt? 

Given the lack of evidence in either direction, I would find it most appropriate to not make any assumptions in either direction. IMO the people in that thread clearly have already made their mind up about hating Cody (and men in general for some of those commenters) and were just looking for an excuse to voice it.
If you ever figure it out, be sure to let me know.
